questions.question: Does executable evidence establish: Assembled HTTP discovery, registration, consent, mocked external Google exchange, token use, refresh, revoke and restart satisfy access boundaries while existing Tasks tools remain available.
Does executable evidence establish: Asynchronous Google events and success/failure responses cannot reactivate disconnected/revoked credentials or grants; transient failures preserve state.
Are failures redacted and changes limited to the reviewed authentication scope?
Does one auth module own each invariant with typed transitions and no duplicated policy?
Do real HTTP and stateful interleavings distinguish owner approval from stored credentials?
Are wrong-owner, replay, resource, scope and cross-client boundaries enforced by production code?
Are atomic persistence, lifecycle limits and deployment defaults explicit and tested?
Does evidence cover every frozen checklist and generated applicable ordering in acceptance-criteria.md, with real production composition and no live path inferred from mocked tests?
